part.text:
Fixed. The hex float path in `write()` (include/fmt/format.h:1801) manually padded using `left_padding_shifts[specs.align]`, which treats an unspecified alignment (`align::none`) as left-aligned — inconsistent with the documented default of right-alignment for numbers.

I replaced the manual padding logic with `write_padded<align::right>` (include/fmt/format.h:1800-1812), which correctly handles the default as right-aligned plus explicit `<`, `>`, and `^`.

Verification:
- `'{:16f}'` and `'{:16a}'` on `4.2f` now both right-align: `'        4.200000'` / `'   0x1.0cccccp+2'`
- Explicit `{:<16a}` and `{:^16a}` still work
- Full test suite passes: 18/18 ctest targets (format-test, format-impl-test, wchar-test, printf-test, etc.)
